name: War of 1812 Timeline of Battles and Events
title: War of 1812 Timeline of Battles and Events
description: Chronological list of battles, naval actions, diplomatic and home-front events of the War of 1812 between the United States and the United Kingdom (1803–1815), with theater and notes.

rows.occurrence: Britain declared war on Napoleonic France
rows.notes: Conflict would grow out to War of the Third Coalition.
Napoleon sold French Louisiana to the U.S. Britain supported deal, hoping to keep U.S. neutral.

rows.occurrence: Quashquame 's treaty with William Henry Harrison
rows.notes: Many Sauk allied with British instead.
England's admiralty court decided seizing certain U.S. merchant ships was legal, escalating tensions.
Major British victory over France
U.S. embargo on importation of certain British goods, in retaliation of the Essex Decision.
Napoleon imposed trade blockade of British Isles.
Intended to stop British impressment of U.S. ships, but President Thomas Jefferson rejected it.
Military and diplomatic naval incident, nearly triggering war between Britain and the U.S.
Britain launched economic warfare against France, straining relations with neutral countries.
Napoleon ordered seizing all ships from neutral countries trading with the British.
U.S. act in retaliation against British and French seizure and impressment of U.S. merchant ships.
France began seizing all U.S. ships in French ports.
U.S. act lifting embargoes on all shipping, except those bound for British and French ports.
U.S.–Shawnee tensions lead to Tecumseh's War.
France orders seizing all U.S. ships in French ports.
U.S. act intended to compel Britain and France to stop seizing U.S. ships.

rows.occurrence: Trade with the United Kingdom closed

rows.notes: Fabricated letters caused diplomatic incident.
Military and diplomatic naval incident, nearly triggering war between Britain and the U.S.
Tecumseh's confederacy defeated.

rows.occurrence: UK Prime Minister Spencer Perceval assassinated.
rows.notes: Pro-war sentiment in Britain decreased, and efforts were made to reconcile with the U.S.
Madison requested the U.S. Congress to declare war.

rows.occurrence: Robert Jenkinson became UK Prime Minister
rows.notes: Some measures to avert war were tried, but they were too little, too late.

rows.occurrence: Castlereagh announced repeal of Orders in Council
rows.notes: News reached U.S. Congress too late to impact U.S. declaration of war on the UK.

rows.occurrence: U.S. declaration of war on UK
Finalized Repeal of Orders in Council

rows.notes: Four U.S. civilians captured a British sergeant and three privates of the 10th Royal Veteran Battalion on Carleton Island, the first POWs of the war.

rows.occurrence: Brits capture schooners Sophia and Island Packet

rows.notes: On the Detroit River, Canadian Provincial Marines under Frédérick Rolette captured U.S. merchant schooner Cuyahoga Packet, containing valuable U.S. military intelligence of William Hull (unaware that war had been declared).

Failed attempt by U.S. general William Hull to invade Upper Canada across the Detroit River at Sandwich. U.S. forces did not capture Fort Amherstburg, and withdrew to Detroit at the news of British reinforcements.
Bloodless capture of Fort Mackinac on Mackinac Island by British regulars, 200 fur traders and 400 Native warriors.
The American brig Nautilus was pursued and captured by the British frigate Shannon off the coast of New Jersey.

rows.occurrence: First Battle of Sacket's Harbor, New York
rows.notes: Failed British naval attack on U.S. naval base Sackets Harbor.

rows.occurrence: Julia versus Earl of Moria and Duke of Gloucester
rows.notes: Standoff between U.S. schooner Julia and two larger British ships. Both sides retired after a three-hour exchange of fire off Elizabethtown, New York.
Minor British victory (including 25 warriors under Tecumseh), ambushing 200 Ohio militiamen at Brownstown, Michigan Territory.

rows.occurrence: Isaac Brock embarked at Port Dover.
rows.notes: British attempt to relieve Amherstburg, besieged by Americans.

Minor U.S. military victory in Michigan Territory, when U.S. troops tried to reopen the supply line between Frenchtown (present-day Monroe) and Detroit was ambushed by British regulars and Tecumseh's native warriors.
Battle off the Azores in which British sloop Alert surrendered to U.S. frigate Essex after an 8-minute engagement.

Massacre of U.S. soldiers and civilians carried out by Potawatomi and Menominee warriors, after Hull ordered the evacuation of Fort Dearborn (Illinois Territory, at present-day Chicago) upon learning the British had captured Fort Mackinac.
Significant U.S. setback. Hull surrendered Detroit (Michigan Territory) without a fight, despite having a larger force that his opponent Isaac Brock.
After battling fewer than 3 hours c. 500 miles southeast of Newfoundland, British frigate HMS Guerriere surrendered to U.S. frigate USS Constitution.

rows.occurrence: The Great Louisiana hurricane struck New Orleans
rows.notes: Both the U.S. and the British fleet damaged.

rows.occurrence: Massacre at Pigeon Roost, Indiana Territory
rows.notes: Kickapoo warriors raided a small settlement, c. 100 miles south of present-day Indianapolis, Indiana.

rows.occurrence: Siege of Fort Harrison, Indiana Territory
rows.notes: A large party of Kickapoo, Miami, Potawatomi, Shawnee and Winnebago warriors from Prophetstown, Indiana Territory attacked the U.S. fort (located on the Wabash River just north of present-day Terre Haute, Indiana) defended by about 60 U.S. soldiers under Zachary Taylor. The Natives withdrew when U.S. reinforcements arrived.
Sauk and Fox warriors failed to capture a fort in Missouri Territory (present-day Fort Madison, Iowa) on the upper Mississippi River.

Failed attempt by about 600 warriors from the Ottawa Nations to infiltrate and attack U.S. garrison at Fort Wayne at the confluence of the Maumee, St. Joseph and St. Mary Rivers in northeastern Indiana Territory.

rows.occurrence: U.S. General Harrison reinforces Fort Wayne
A. C. Muir 's British expedition at Fort Wayne

rows.notes: U.S. troops threatened the forced displacement of Native American peoples in Ashland County, Ohio, against which they resisted. U.S. victory.
Failed attempt of U.S. from Ogdensburg, New York to intercept a British supply convoy of forty bateaux coming up the St. Lawrence River.
Successful raid by American troops from Sackets Harbor on the British depot at Gananoque, Upper Canada.

rows.occurrence: First British raid at Charlotte, New York
rows.notes: British raid seizing U.S. merchantman Lady Murray and a smaller boat, with no U.S. resistance.
Failed British amphibious attack on Ogdensburg, a supply transshipment point on the St. Lawrence River, repelled by U.S. artillery.

rows.occurrence: Winchester 's U.S. army arrives near Fort Defiance
U.S. Navy captures British brigs Caledonia and Detroit
rows.notes: At Fort Erie, Upper Canada, 100 U.S. soldiers raided across the Niagara River from Buffalo and captured two Provincial Marine brigs. The Caledonia was recovered, but the Detroit ran aground and was scuttled to prevent British recapture.
Major U.S. defeat when Stephen Van Rensselaer tried to capture Queenston, Upper Canada on the west side of the Niagara River. Isaac Brock was killed in battle.

Battle c. 300 miles north of Bermuda, seriously damaging both sloops. British sloop surrendered after U.S. sloop boarded it. Later that day, with both ship crews making repairs, HMS Poictiers captured USS Wasp and recaptured Frolic.
Temporary victory by New York State Militia who captured a British post at Akwesasne (St. Regis). British troops recaptured it and the nearby U.S. post at French Mills a month later.

rows.occurrence: USS United States vs HMS Macedonian
rows.notes: 2-hour battle c. 500 miles west of Canary Islands; British frigate Macedonian surrendered to U.S. frigate United States, and was acquired by the U. S. Navy.

rows.occurrence: British blockade South Carolina and Georgia

rows.notes: Isaac Chauncey attacks Kingston Harbour
U.S. attack ordered by Harrison on an unoccupied Indian settlement near the junction of the Tippecanoe and Wabash Rivers north of present-day Lafayette, Indiana.

rows.occurrence: Battle of Lacolle Mills, Lower Canada
rows.notes: Confused U.S. troops attacked each other, then were attacked by British/loyalist troops. U.S. troops retreated to Champlain, and Henry Dearborn called off his planned invasion of Lower Canada.
At Wildcat Creek (Indiana), Native American forces supported by the British defeated the U.S.

Pursuit and capture of U.S. brig Vixen, c. 90 miles east of St. Augustine, Florida, by British frigate Southampton. Both vessels were wrecked on a shoal near Concepcíon Island on November 27; the crews were rescued and taken to Jamaica.
British victory at French Mills, New York.

rows.occurrence: Battle of Frenchman's Creek, Upper Canada
rows.notes: U.S. raid across the Niagara River, spiking British artillery at Red House to enable a future U.S. landing, but failing to destroy a bridge over Frenchman's Creek to prevent British reinforcements.

rows.occurrence: Smyth's failed invasion of Upper Canada
rows.notes: U.S. officer Alexander Smyth tried and failed to get his invasion force assembled to cross the Niagara River and invade Upper Canada, but cancelled the entire operation.

rows.occurrence: William Eustis resigns as U.S. Secretary of War
James Monroe serves as U.S. Secretary of War

rows.notes: Part of a U.S. expedition against Delaware and Miami villages where the Mississinewa River flows into the Wabash River near present-day Marion, Indiana.

rows.occurrence: British blockade Chesapeake and Delaware Bay

rows.notes: 2.5-hour battle off the coast of Brazil during which British 38-gun fifth-rate Java suffered such serious damage that its captain ordered it scuttled.

rows.occurrence: Paul Hamilton resigns as Secretary of the Navy
William Jones serves as Secretary of the Navy
John Armstrong serves as Secretary of War

rows.notes: U.S. victory.

rows.occurrence: 104th Regiment commences march from Fredericton to Upper Canada
rows.notes: 104th Regiment of Foot (New Brunswick Fencibles)

rows.occurrence: USS Essex rounds Cape Horn, preys on British whaling ships
Admiral George Cockburn 's squadron arrives in Lynnhaven Bay
Sir James Lucas Yeo appointed Commander-in-chief of the Lake Squadrons
Oliver Hazard Perry constructs Lake Erie fleet
British blockade from Long Island to Mississippi
Commerce raids begin in Chesapeake Bay

rows.notes: Indecisive clash between Shawnee and U.S. forces.
Lewes, Delaware bombarded by British
U.S. forces defeat pro-British Native Americans near Fort Lamotte on the Wabash River.
At the site of present-day Toronto, Upper Canada.

rows.occurrence: James Lucas Yeo arrives at Quebec
British blockade middle states and southern states
John Harvey retreats to Burlington Heights
George Prevost and James Lucas Yeo attacked Sackets Harbor
Capture of USS Chesapeake by HMS Shannon
Capture of U.S. sloops Growler and Eagle near Île aux Noix
British vessels repulsed at Burlington, Vermont
Commodore Barclay 's squadron appears off of Cleveland, Ohio
USS Constellation1797 (6) attempts capture of blockading vessels off Hampton, Virginia
Privateer Teazer blown up in Mahone Bay, Nova Scotia
Final siege of Fort Madison begins, fort defeated sometime in September
Privateers Atlas and Anaconda taken by the British at the port of Ocracoke, North Carolina
General Henry Procter quits the siege of Fort Meigs

rows.notes: General Henry Proctor 's assault fails

rows.occurrence: Commodore Oliver Hazard Perry sails fleet into Lake Erie
U.S. schooners Hamilton and Scourge founder on Lake Ontario
Naval engagement ships Julia and Pert captured

rows.notes: Red Sticks capture fort and kill its U.S. soldiers and civilians.
Key U.S. victory
U.S. victory

rows.occurrence: William Henry Harrison lands in Canada, Detroit liberated
Great Britain offers the United States peace negotiations
James Wilkinson 's flotilla runs past the batteries at Fort Wellington
Funeral of General Covington at French Mills
James Wilkinson 's army goes into winter quarters
British extend naval blockade along U.S. coast
Major General David Adams burned Nuyaka
British destroy Lewiston, Fort Schlosser, Black Rock, and Buffalo
Battles of Emuckfaw and Enotachopo Creek
Napoleon abdicates French throne for the first time
United States repeals Embargo Act and Nonimportation Act
British extend blockade to New England
General William Clark leaves St. Louis for Prairie du Chien
Lieutenant Colonel Robert McDouall relieves Fort Mackinac
William Clark establishes Fort Shelby at Prairie du Chien
Major William McKay 's expedition leaves Fort Mackinac
Treaty of Greenville US and western tribes ally against Great Britain
Sinclair 's squadron arrives off Mackinac Island
Schooner Nancy warned of Fort Mackinac blockade
Creek people sign treaty at Fort Jackson
Capture of USS Somers and USS Ohio on Lake Erie
Part of Sinclair 's squadron arrives at Nottawasaga River

rows.notes: British capture Alexandria, Virginia.

rows.occurrence: George Prevost moves south toward Plattsburgh
John Armstrong, Jr. resigns and James Monroe becomes Secretary of War
Fort Johnson built, abandoned one month later
Francis Scott Key writes " The Star-Spangled Banner "
Counterattack at Siege of Fort Erie
British squadron captures USS General Armstrong
United Kingdom offers peace on basis of uti possidetis
British fleet sail from Jamaica for New Orleans
United Kingdom drops demands for uti possidetis
British overwhelm American gunboats on Lake Borgne
United States adopts additional internal taxation
British land their troops below New Orleans
Andrew Jackson surprise-attacks the British camp at Villeré Plantation

rows.notes: A three-hour cannon duel between 4 British batteries, including heavy naval guns and a rocket battery, and 7 U.S. batteries in Andrew Jackson 's line of defense. The British ceased fire when their artillery ran out of ammunition and failed to breach Jackson's ramparts.
Most lop-sided U.S. victory of the war: British had 2,037 casualties (KIA, WIA, POW), Americans around 71.
Failed British attempt to dislodge U.S. forces at Fort St. Philip, Louisiana that would have blocked efforts to supply the British in New Orleans.
British victory.
British warship HMS Endymion captured U.S. frigate President attempting to break out of the British blockade of New York City. The President was severely damaged, and surrendered.

Diversionary expedition of Cochrane's Gulf Coast campaign (May 1814 – Feb 1815) to the southeastern U.S. coast. Brits under George Cockburn occupied Cumberland Island, a fort and the town of St. Marys in Jan 1815, effectively blockading Savannah, Charleston and other coastal areas. Cockburn left on March 18 after learning of the Treaty of Ghent.

rows.occurrence: United States adopts second enemy trade law

rows.notes: Last Gulf Coast theater battle. British forces retreating from New Orleans landed on Dauphine Island and recaptured nearby Fort Bowyer, but withdrew upon news of the Treaty of Ghent.

rows.occurrence: United States ratifies Treaty of Ghent
United States rejects First Bank of the United States proposal
USS Constitution versus HMS Cyane and HMS Levant
rows.notes: U.S. frigate Constitution captured two British sixth-rates Cyane and Levant about 200 miles northeast of Madeira. The Levant was later recaptured by British frigate Leander.

rows.occurrence: US privateer Chasseur versus HMS St Lawrence
rows.notes: U.S. privateer Chasseur captured British schooner St. Lawrence, which was carrying news of the signing of the Treaty of Ghent to the British, in the Gulf of Mexico.

rows.occurrence: Napoleon escaped from Elba, triggering the Hundred Days

rows.notes: British squadron under Collier recaptured British warship Levant as Constitution tried to flee with its two prizes from the harbor at Porto Playa in the Cape Verde Islands.
U.S. sloop Hornet captured British sloop Penguin in a battle near Tristan de Cunha.

rows.occurrence: Escape from H M Dartmoor Prison

rows.notes: Last land battle of war, between Missouri Rangers and Sauk warriors led by Black Hawk, near Cuivre River's mouth, Missouri Territory.

rows.occurrence: USS Peacock versus East India Company ship Nautilus
rows.notes: Final naval engagement of the war. U.S. sloop Peacock fired on and seriously damaged East India brig Nautilus in the Straits of Sunda. British captain Boyce informed the U.S. ship commander the Treaty of Ghent had been signed on Dec 24, 1814, but the U.S. ship opened fire anyway.
